Question Paper  
Exam Date & Time: 18-Nov-2025 (02:00 PM - 05:00 PM)  
  
  
  MANIPAL ACADEMY OF HIGHER EDUCATION  
  MANIPAL INSTITUTE OF TECHNOLOGY - BENGALURU  
  SEVENTH SEMESTER B.TECH. DEGREE EXAMINATIONS - NOVEMBER 2025  
  Blockchain Architecture Design and Use Cases [NPT_4128]  
Marks: 50                                                                                                    Duration: 180 mins.  
  
  PART-A  
Answer all the questions.  
  
1)                Discover the lifecycle of chaincode deployment in Fabric from packaging to committing transactions. (3)  
  
  
  A)                                                      Course Outcome: "CO5" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
  B)           Identify how Fabric handles membership service providers (MSPs) and ordering nodes in a              (3)  
  consortium network.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO1" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
  C)           Analyze scalability and performance trade-offs between on-premise Fabric and IBM Blockchain          (4)  
  Cloud implementations.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO1" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
2)                Examine the sequence of chaincode lifecycle management - from installation to endorsement policy (3)  
  enforcement and instantiation on channels.  
  A)  
  Course Outcome: "CO2" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
  B)           Distinguish how private data collections enhance confidentiality in Fabric without compromising      (3)  
  network transparency.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO2" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
  C)           Design the deployment workflow of a Fabric network on AWS Managed Blockchain vis-à-vis               (4)  
  manual setup using Docker and Kubernetes.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO2" / Cognitive Level: "Create"  
  
3)                Evaluate how blockchain enables real-time cross-border payments and reduces settlement risk.         (3)  
  
  
  A)                                                         Course Outcome: "CO4" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
  B)           Elaborate the use of smart contracts in automating trade settlements in global finance.              (3)  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO5" / Cognitive Level: "Create"  
  
  C)           Evaluate the impact of TradeLens on international logistics efficiency and transparency.             (4)  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO3" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
  Page #1

4)                        Defend how blockchain reduces documentation delays in global trade logistics.                         (3)  
  
  
  A)                                                              Course Outcome: "CO4" / Cognitive Level: "Evaluate"  
  
  B)                Classify the architectural flow of TradeLens and its key modules.                                     (3)  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO3" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
  C)                Criticize how blockchain networks like Hyperledger Fabric transform customs verification systems.     (4)  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO3" / Cognitive Level: "Evaluate"  
  
5)                        Examine tokenization in trade finance and analyze how smart contracts automate Letter of Credit       (4)  
  processes.  
  A)  
  Course Outcome: "CO3" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
  B)                Identify how TradeLens leverages IoT sensors and blockchain analytics to enhance maritime             (3)  
  logistics visibility.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO3" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
  C)                Analyze the role of provenance data in ensuring ethical sourcing and authenticity in global supply    (3)  
  chains.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO3" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"
